"The crust under the major mountain systems, such as the Himalayas, is about 70 km thick. The density of material increases from the crust to the core. The crust is thicker under the continents than under the oceans."
(i) The upper portion of the mantle, the main source of magma, is called the: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'lithosphere' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The core is very dense. (1)
items.answer: (i) asthenosphere (ii) The crust together with the uppermost solid part of the mantle, between 10 and 200 km thick. (iii) It is made of very heavy materials, mainly nickel and iron.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) asthenosphere (ii) The crust together with the uppermost solid part of the mantle, between 10 and 200 km thick. (iii) It is made of very heavy materials, mainly nickel and iron.

items.stem: In the study of sources of information about the interior of the earth, the term 'indirect sources' refers to:
items.answer: Evidence such as temperature, pressure, density, meteors, gravity, magnetism and seismic waves used to infer the interior
items.markingKey: (c) 'indirect sources' means evidence such as temperature, pressure, density, meteors, gravity, magnetism and seismic waves used to infer the interior.
options: The part of the interior beneath the crust, extending from the Moho discontinuity to a depth of 2,900 km
Materials obtained directly from the earth's interior, such as rocks from mines, drilling and volcanic eruptions
Evidence such as temperature, pressure, density, meteors, gravity, magnetism and seismic waves used to infer the interior
A large, gently sloping volcano formed mostly of fluid basalt lava, as in Hawaii

items.stem:
Statement: Surface waves are the most destructive.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: They travel along the surface and cause the greatest displacement of rocks and structures.
items.markingKey: (a) They travel along the surface and cause the greatest displacement of rocks and structures.
options: They travel along the surface and cause the greatest displacement of rocks and structures.
It is made of very heavy materials, mainly nickel and iron.
An earthquake under the ocean floor can displace a large volume of sea water.
The waves are refracted or blocked by the materials of the interior so that some areas receive none.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the structure of the earth is correct?
items.answer: The density of material increases from the crust to the core.
items.markingKey: (d) The others are wrong: It includes the crust and only the uppermost solid part of the mantle. Oceanic crust is about 5 km thick, continental crust about 30 km. The inner core is solid; the outer core is liquid.
options: The oceanic crust is thicker than the continental crust.
The inner core of the earth is liquid.
The lithosphere includes the entire mantle.
The density of material increases from the crust to the core.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on volcanoes and volcanic landforms and answer the questions that follow.
"Volcanic landforms are divided into extrusive and intrusive forms. Volcanoes are classified on the basis of the nature of eruption and the form developed at the surface. Mid-ocean ridge volcanoes occur along a long chain of mountains in the oceans."
(i) A wavy mass of intrusive rock found at the base of synclines or the top of anticlines is a: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'caldera' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Shield volcanoes have gentle slopes. (1)
items.answer: (i) phacolith (ii) The most explosive type of volcano, which collapses on itself after eruption rather than building a tall structure. (iii) They are formed of very fluid basalt lava that spreads over large distances.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) phacolith (ii) The most explosive type of volcano, which collapses on itself after eruption rather than building a tall structure. (iii) They are formed of very fluid basalt lava that spreads over large distances.

items.stem:
Statement: The core is very dense.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: It is made of very heavy materials, mainly nickel and iron.
items.markingKey: (d) It is made of very heavy materials, mainly nickel and iron.
options: Mountain ranges have deep 'roots' of crustal material beneath them.
The waves are refracted or blocked by the materials of the interior so that some areas receive none.
It is the main source of the magma that reaches the surface.
It is made of very heavy materials, mainly nickel and iron.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about volcanoes and volcanic landforms is correct?
items.answer: Mid-ocean ridge volcanoes occur along a long chain of mountains in the oceans.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: Batholiths form by cooling of magma in the deeper crust. A dyke is vertical; a sill is near-horizontal. Calderas are the most explosive; shield volcanoes erupt fluid basalt lava.
options: Batholiths are formed on the surface of the earth.
Shield volcanoes are the most explosive volcanoes.
Mid-ocean ridge volcanoes occur along a long chain of mountains in the oceans.
A dyke is a horizontal body of intrusive rock.

items.stem:
Statement: Batholiths become exposed on the surface.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: The overlying rocks are removed by denudation over long periods.
items.markingKey: (c) The overlying rocks are removed by denudation over long periods.
options: It is made of very heavy materials, mainly nickel and iron.
Their lava is cooler and more viscous, so gases build up and erupt violently.
The overlying rocks are removed by denudation over long periods.
They are formed of very fluid basalt lava that spreads over large distances.

items.stem: "Tsunamis can follow earthquakes." Examine this statement with reference to earthquakes and earthquake waves.
items.answer: The statement is valid. An earthquake under the ocean floor can displace a large volume of sea water.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (an earthquake under the ocean floor can displace a large volume of sea water.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the structure of the earth:
I. The crust under the major mountain systems, such as the Himalayas, is about 70 km thick.
II. The lithosphere includes the entire mantle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is incorrect: It includes the crust and only the uppermost solid part of the mantle.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem: What is meant by 'indirect sources' in the context of sources of information about the interior of the earth?
items.answer: Evidence such as temperature, pressure, density, meteors, gravity, magnetism and seismic waves used to infer the interior.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: indirect sources correctly explained as evidence such as temperature, pressure, density, meteors, gravity, magnetism and seismic waves used to infer the interior.

items.stem: Name the types of earthquakes and mention one cause of each.
items.answer: Tectonic – sliding along faults; volcanic – in active volcanic areas; collapse – collapse of mine roofs; explosion – nuclear or chemical explosions; reservoir-induced – large dams.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Tectonic – sliding along faults; volcanic – in active volcanic areas; collapse – collapse of mine roofs; explosion – nuclear or chemical explosions; reservoir-induced – large dams.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about earthquakes and earthquake waves is NOT correct?
items.answer: The epicentre is the point inside the earth where energy is released.
items.markingKey: (c) It is incorrect. That is the focus; the epicentre is the point on the surface above it.
options: Earthquakes are caused by the release of energy along faults.
The fact that S-waves do not pass through the outer core shows that it is liquid.
The epicentre is the point inside the earth where energy is released.
The shadow zone of S-waves is much larger than that of P-waves.

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to sources of information about the interior of the earth.
(a) Give a reason for the following: Meteors are useful for studying the interior. (1)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "Mining provides information from the core of the earth." (2)
items.answer: (a) Their material and structure are similar to those of the earth's interior. (b) Mining and drilling give information only from shallow depths.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (a) 1 for the reason – their material and structure are similar to those of the earth's interior. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – Mining and drilling give information only from shallow depths. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on sources of information about the interior of the earth and answer the questions that follow.
"Seismic activity is the most important source of information about the earth's interior. Most of our knowledge about the earth's interior is based on estimates and inferences. Magma from volcanic eruptions gives information about materials deep inside the earth."
(i) Which of the following is an indirect source of information about the earth's interior? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'gravity anomaly' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Gravity anomalies tell us about the crust. (1)
items.answer: (i) Seismic activity (ii) The difference between the expected and the observed value of gravity, which indicates the distribution of mass in the crust. (iii) The gravitation force varies with the distribution of mass in the material of the crust.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Seismic activity (ii) The difference between the expected and the observed value of gravity, which indicates the distribution of mass in the crust. (iii) The gravitation force varies with the distribution of mass in the material of the crust.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about volcanoes and volcanic landforms:
I. Shield volcanoes are made mostly of basalt, a very fluid lava.
II. Volcanic landforms are divided into extrusive and intrusive forms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The crust is thickest under the Himalayas.
Reason (R): Mining and drilling give direct information, but only from shallow depths.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (b) Both statements are true, but R deals with a different point and does not explain A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The most common type of earthquake is the:
items.answer: tectonic earthquake
items.markingKey: (d) tectonic earthquake.
options: volcanic earthquake
collapse earthquake
explosion earthquake
tectonic earthquake

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about sources of information about the interior of the earth is correct?
items.answer: Seismic activity is the most important source of information about the earth's interior.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: Gravity is greater near the poles and varies with the distribution of mass. Mining and drilling give information only from shallow depths. Temperature, pressure and density increase with depth.
options: Temperature decreases as we go deeper into the earth.
Mining provides information from the core of the earth.
Seismic activity is the most important source of information about the earth's interior.
Gravity is the same everywhere on the earth's surface.

items.stem: The following statement about earthquakes and earthquake waves is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The Richter scale measures the intensity of an earthquake."
items.answer: It measures magnitude; the Mercalli scale measures intensity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (It measures magnitude; the Mercalli scale measures intensity.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the structure of the earth and answer the questions that follow.
"The asthenosphere in the upper mantle is the main source of magma that reaches the surface during volcanic eruptions. The inner core is in a solid state, while the outer core is liquid. The crust under the major mountain systems, such as the Himalayas, is about 70 km thick."
(i) The core–mantle boundary lies at a depth of about: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'asthenosphere' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The core is very dense. (1)
items.answer: (i) 2,900 km (ii) The upper portion of the mantle, extending up to about 400 km, which is the main source of magma. (iii) It is made of very heavy materials, mainly nickel and iron.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) 2,900 km (ii) The upper portion of the mantle, extending up to about 400 km, which is the main source of magma. (iii) It is made of very heavy materials, mainly nickel and iron.
